small_guidance:
- The atomic_add into a zero-initialized accumulator across N-tiles is the correctness bug source: BLOCK_N tiles that don't align to N can produce wrong reductions, but more critically the kernel was tested with non-deterministic input (torch.seed in get_inputs) — verify partial sums; switch to a single-program-per-row reduction (grid = (M,)) with an internal K-loop over N in BLOCK_N chunks to avoid atomics entirely.
- Set BLOCK_N as a multiple of KERNEL_SIZE (guaranteed since N=32768, KS=2) and ensure BLOCK_N divides N exactly so no masked tail with -inf needs the where-replace; drop the neg_inf->0 hack which can mask real bugs.
- Tune BLOCK_N in {2048, 4096, 8192} with num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4 since each row reads 32768 fp32 (128KB) and benefits from deeper pipelining.
large_guidance:
- Fuse the entire pipeline (matmul + bias + maxpool + sum + scale) into one Triton GEMM-style kernel: one program per row M, tiled K-loop over in_features computing a full (1, out_features) row of y in registers/SMEM is infeasible at N=32768, so instead do one program per (row, N-tile) computing a BLOCK_N slice of y via tl.dot over K, then immediately maxpool-pairwise-reduce-sum that slice and atomic_add the scaled partial. This eliminates the 128×32768 intermediate write/read.
- Alternatively keep cuBLAS for the GEMM but make the post-kernel persistent: one program per row, loop over N in chunks, accumulate sum-of-pairwise-max in a register scalar, single non-atomic store at the end. Removes atomics and the zeros() init.
- For the fused-GEMM path use BLOCK_M=8 or 16 (batch=128), BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=32-64, num_warps=8, num_stages=3, with epilogue: reshape (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N) -> (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N/2, 2), max axis=2, sum axis=1, scale, atomic_add to out[m].
